testPolicy.text: All first-year applicants must submit results from at least one SAT and/or ACT in order to be considered for admission. Self-reported scores are accepted and highly recommended; Georgia Tech uses the highest EBRW and Math section scores (SAT) and highest English, Math and Reading (ACT). CLT, AP and IB are optional and do not replace the requirement.
testPolicy.since: CDS 2025-26 C8A marks SAT or ACT 'required to be considered for admission' for fall 2027 applicants

cost.totalIncludes: First-year, on campus, two semesters: tuition + mandatory student fees + books, course materials, supplies and equipment + housing allowance + standard food service plan + personal/miscellaneous + transportation allowance. Out-of-country students: tuition 35,610, fees 1,716, total 56,520.

aidPromise.text: G. Wayne Clough Georgia Tech Promise Scholarship: academically qualified in-state students with family incomes below $55,500 can earn a Georgia Tech degree debt free.

deadlines.early: October 15 (Early Action 1, Georgia students only) or November 2 (Early Action 2, non-Georgia and international students); both non-binding

facts.text: For fall 2025, Georgia Tech admitted 3,691 of 12,527 Georgia applicants but only 4,513 of 44,596 out-of-state applicants and 716 of 9,758 international applicants.
Early Action is split by residency: EA1 (October 15) is for Georgia students, EA2 (November 2) for everyone else, and both are non-binding.
Merit scholarships such as the Stamps President's Scholars Program require applying through an Early Action plan.
An SAT or ACT score is mandatory for every first-year applicant.
A non-resident first-year on campus has a 2026-27 cost of attendance of 55,314 against 30,928 for a Georgia resident; tuition is 34,604 against 10,618.
In-state students from families earning under $55,500 can graduate debt free through the Georgia Tech Promise scholarship.

notes: Cycle from CDS 2025-26 C1 (44,517 + 22,363 + 1 = 66,881 applied; 4,937 + 3,983 + 1 = 8,921 admitted; 2,340 + 1,730 + 1 = 4,071 enrolled); the IRP page links revision R4 of 3 June 2026 (an earlier R3 of 30 March 2026 is cited by third parties). C21 ED: No; C22 EA closing 11/1, notification 1/31 for the fall 2025 cycle, not restrictive. The financial aid page also publishes an 'Estimated 2027-2028 Cost of Attendance' (first-year Georgia resident on campus 31,628: tuition 10,618, fees 1,496, books 800, housing 8,718, food 6,610, personal 2,800, transport 586; out-of-state 55,018 with tuition 33,596), lower out-of-state tuition than 2026-27; the approved 2026-27 budget is recorded as cost and the 2027-28 estimate is kept here only. CDS G1 2026-27 matches (tuition 10,618 / 34,604, fees 1,516). No official fall 2026 class numbers found.
